title: ERBE VIO 300 Series - Module Communication Errors Between Generator and Accessories
description: Guide for troubleshooting communication errors between ERBE VIO 300 generator and accessories, focusing on external causes before internal module failure.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Unit
steps.instructions: Turn off the ESU and unplug it from the wall. Wait 30–60 seconds, then reconnect and power on. Why: Some communication errors are transient and resolve after a full power cycle.

steps.title: Verify Power Source and Outlet
steps.instructions: Confirm the outlet is supplying stable power using a meter or a verified device. Ensure the ESU is connected to the correct voltage and a properly grounded outlet. Why: Fluctuating voltage or grounding issues can cause modules to fail to communicate properly.

steps.title: Inspect and Reseat All Cables
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the accessory cables, including footswitch, handpiece, and HF modules. Check for bent pins, corrosion, fraying, or loose connections. Why: Poor electrical contact is a common cause of communication errors.

steps.title: Test Accessories Individually
steps.instructions: Connect one accessory at a time to isolate the problematic module. Replace suspected faulty accessories with a known working one. Why: This identifies whether the error is in the generator or the accessory itself.

steps.title: Check for Error Codes and Messages
steps.instructions: Record the exact communication error messages displayed by the ESU. Refer to ERBE’s quick reference or internal troubleshooting chart for specific error codes. Why: Some errors indicate specific module failures or cable faults.

steps.title: Verify Firmware Compatibility
steps.instructions: Ensure the generator firmware and accessory firmware versions are compatible. Check ERBE documentation for required updates. Why: Mismatched firmware can prevent proper module communication.

steps.title: Inspect Module Connectors and Ports
steps.instructions: Look for debris, dirt, or damage inside the module connectors. Clean gently with approved contact cleaner if needed. Why: Contaminants can interrupt communication signals.

CCR.Complaint: Generator displays ‘Module Communication Error’ when footswitch and handpiece are connected.
CCR.Cause: Observed loose handpiece connector and intermittent footswitch response; error persists after power cycle and cable reseating.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated all cables and tested accessories individually. Issue persisted; ESU labeled Out of Service and sent to ERBE for bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Physical inspection of connectors completed: Yes / No

title: ERBE VIO 300 Series - APC Module Ignition Failure or Gas Flow Errors
description: Guide to troubleshoot APC module ignition failure or gas flow errors on ERBE VIO 300 ESUs, focusing on external causes first.

steps.title: Verify Power and Status
steps.instructions: Ensure the VIO 300 is powered on and no global errors are displayed. Check that the device has completed its self-test and is ready for use. Why: APC module ignition requires proper generator initialization.

steps.title: Check Argon Gas Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm the argon cylinder is open and has sufficient pressure. Inspect the cylinder valve for blockage or damage. Why: Insufficient gas pressure will prevent module ignition.

steps.title: Inspect Gas Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify all tubing from the gas source to the APC module is securely connected and free from kinks. Check for leaks using a non-flammable leak detector or listen for hissing. Why: Leaks or restricted flow cause ignition failure and gas flow errors.

steps.title: Confirm APC Module Connection
steps.instructions: Ensure the APC handpiece or module is correctly seated in the ESU port. Inspect the connector for dirt, debris, or bent pins. Why: Poor electrical contact prevents proper communication between generator and module.

steps.title: Check Module Settings and Mode
steps.instructions: Verify the generator settings match the APC handpiece requirements (power, flow rate). Confirm the APC module is selected in the generator menu. Why: Incorrect settings can simulate flow errors or prevent ignition.

steps.title: Perform a Test with Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Swap in a verified working APC handpiece and tubing. Observe if ignition succeeds. Why: Confirms whether the problem is with the module, accessory, or gas supply.

steps.title: Monitor Device Indicators and Alarms
steps.instructions: Check generator display for error codes, flow readings, or warnings during attempted ignition. Note any unusual LED behavior on the APC module. Why: Provides clues for escalation or repair.

CCR.Complaint: APC module will not ignite; gas flow error displayed.
CCR.Cause: Observed kinked argon tubing and module connector partially seated.
CCR.Resolution: Straightened tubing, fully seated module; APC ignition successful.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (ready, out of service)

title: ERBE VIO 300 Series - Footswitch or Instrument Activation Failure
description: Guide for troubleshooting footswitch or instrument activation failures on ERBE VIO 300 ESUs, focusing on external causes before internal module issues.

steps.title: Verify Device Power and Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the VIO 300 is plugged into a live, grounded outlet. Check that the device powers on normally and displays the main menu. Why: Activation failures can appear if the unit is not fully powered.

steps.title: Inspect Footswitch and Instrument Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the footswitch and any active instruments. Examine connectors for bent pins, corrosion, or debris. Ensure connectors are fully seated and secure. Why: Poor connections are a common cause of intermittent activation.

steps.title: Test with a Known Good Footswitch or Instrument
steps.instructions: Swap the footswitch or instrument with one verified to function properly. Test activation functions for each mode. Why: Isolates whether the issue lies with the accessory or the generator.

steps.title: Check for Accessory Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm the instrument or footswitch is compatible with the VIO 300 model and current software version. Why: Incompatible accessories may not trigger activation signals correctly.

steps.title: Inspect Generator Settings and Mode Selection
steps.instructions: Ensure the correct mode is selected for the connected instrument (e.g., APC, CUT, COAG). Verify energy output settings are within safe, expected ranges. Why: Some instruments only activate under certain modes.

steps.title: Check Software and Communication Status
steps.instructions: Observe the display for any communication warnings or error messages between generator and accessory. If errors appear, note the code and proceed to escalate. Why: Communication errors can prevent activation even when connections appear correct.

steps.title: Perform a Basic Self-Test / Diagnostic
steps.instructions: Use the VIO 300 built-in test function (if available) to verify footswitch or instrument recognition. Why: Confirms if the generator correctly detects the accessory.

CCR.Complaint: Footswitch fails to activate energy delivery; instrument triggers not responding.
CCR.Cause: Footswitch connector slightly loose; generator recognizes no accessory input.
CCR.Resolution: Reconnected footswitch securely; verified operation. Device functional.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested with known good device
Cables and connectors inspected or swapped
Footswitch functionality verified on a separate generator
Generator display messages or error codes

title: ERBE VIO 300 Series - Touchscreen or Control Panel Responsiveness Issues
description: Guide to troubleshoot unresponsive or intermittently responsive touchscreen/control panel on ERBE VIO 300 ESU, focusing on external causes first.

steps.title: Ensure Safe Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is not in active patient use. Move the patient to another ESU if necessary. Rationale: Prevents patient harm during testing.

steps.title: Check Power Connection
steps.instructions: Verify the power cord is securely connected to a known working outlet. Confirm the voltage matches specifications for the ESU. Observe the power indicator lights for proper startup. Rationale: Unstable or insufficient power can cause touchscreen lag or failure.

steps.title: Inspect Touchscreen Surface and Cleanliness
steps.instructions: Check for smudges, debris, or moisture on the touchscreen. Clean with a soft, lint-free cloth and approved cleaning solution. Rationale: Contaminants can interfere with capacitive or resistive touchscreen detection.

steps.title: Verify External Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect all accessories (handpieces, footswitches, APC modules). Ensure no pins are bent or ports damaged. Rationale: Some ESU touchscreens may become unresponsive if accessory detection fails.

steps.title: Check for Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Ensure there is no strong electromagnetic interference nearby (e.g., MRI units, high-power cautery). Keep the device on a stable surface; extreme vibrations can affect control panel sensors.

steps.title: Soft Reset / Reboot
steps.instructions: Power down the ESU completely. Wait 30–60 seconds, then restart. Observe if the touchscreen responds normally during boot-up. Rationale: Temporary software glitches can affect responsiveness.

steps.title: Firmware/Software Check
steps.instructions: Confirm the ESU is running the latest approved firmware. If outdated, schedule a controlled software update per manufacturer instructions. Rationale: Known firmware bugs can affect touchscreen functionality.

CCR.Complaint: Touchscreen is unresponsive and fails to register mode changes or energy activation.
CCR.Cause: Observed touchscreen lag persists after power cycle; no external debris or accessory faults detected.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent for manufacturer evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Power indicator lights normal during startup

title: ERBE VIO 300 Series - Output Regulation Errors or System Alarms
description: Guide to troubleshoot ERBE VIO 300 ESU when generator displays output regulation errors, inconsistent energy delivery, or system alarms, focusing on external causes first.

steps.title: Verify Power Supply and Outlet
steps.instructions: Ensure the ESU is plugged into a properly grounded outlet. Check for tripped breakers or outlet power using a calibrated outlet tester. Why: Inconsistent voltage can cause regulation errors or alarms.

steps.title: Inspect the Main Power Cable and Connections
steps.instructions: Check for frayed or damaged cords. Confirm all connections are fully seated. Why: Loose or damaged cables can trigger internal fault detection.

steps.title: Check Footswitch, Handpiece, and Accessory Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure footswitch is fully connected and the cable is not damaged. Inspect handpiece for proper seating and absence of visible damage. Why: Improper accessory connections can cause false output errors.

steps.title: Verify Generator Settings and Mode Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct energy mode (e.g., cut, coag, APC) is selected. Ensure any programmed presets are within safe parameters. Why: Mismatched settings or presets may trigger alarms.

steps.title: Perform a Self-Test / Built-in Safety Check
steps.instructions: Follow the generator’s on-screen self-test procedure. Document any fault codes or alarm messages displayed. Why: The self-test identifies internal issues without disassembly.

steps.title: Check for Environmental Factors
steps.instructions: Ensure the ESU is not in a high-humidity area or near magnetic interference. Confirm adequate cooling and airflow; remove any obstructions. Why: Environmental conditions can affect regulation circuits and trigger alarms.

CCR.Complaint: Generator displays output regulation error when attempting coag mode.
CCR.Cause: No external power, handpiece connected intermittently, and footswitch cable partially loose.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected power source, reseated all connections, ran self-test to confirm error cleared. Device returned to service.

helpfulDetails: All cables inspected and swapped if needed
Final device status (Ready for use or Out of Service)

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - APC Ignition Is Delayed or Argon Flow Is Unstable
description: Troubleshoots delayed APC ignition or unstable argon delivery by checking gas supply, applicators, tubing, connections, setup, and workstation communication.

steps.title: 1. Stop Unreliable APC Treatment
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unstable APC delivery while a patient depends on the system. Transition to another verified APC system or approved clinical alternative. Expected outcome: The patient is not exposed to unpredictable ignition or gas delivery.

steps.title: 2. Define the APC Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether plasma fails to ignite, ignition is delayed, argon flow appears intermittent, the issue occurs with one applicator, or APC functionality is unavailable entirely. Expected outcome: The problem is separated into accessory, gas-flow, activation, or system-level behavior.

steps.title: 3. Verify APC Workstation Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the APC component is powered, recognized by the VIO 3, and not showing an unresolved system alarm. Verify the intended APC program and instrument are selected. ERBE's VIO/APC workstation integrates APC selection and activation through the VIO interface. [Exceptional](https://www.exceptional.erbe-med.com/index.php?utm_source=chatgpt.com) Expected outcome: The APC component is powered, communicating, and available for normal operation.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Argon Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm the installed argon source is the correct approved supply, is connected securely, is open when required, and is not depleted or obviously compromised. Do not adjust gas-system regulators or internal pneumatic components unless specifically authorized and trained. Expected outcome: An adequate approved argon source is available to the APC system.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Gas Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible gas hoses and connectors for kinks, crushing, incomplete seating, visible damage, contamination, or incorrect routing. Expected outcome: The external argon path is unobstructed and securely connected.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the APC Applicator and Cable
steps.instructions: Verify that the applicator is compatible with the APC system and inspect the connection, cable, and distal accessory for visible damage or blockage. ERBE specifies compatible APC instruments with integrated filtering for APC 3 use. [register.erbe-med.com](https://register.erbe-med.com/productfinder/Marketingmaterialien/80115-501_ERBE_EN_VIO_3_V_14x__D247327.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) Expected outcome: The APC accessory is appropriate, undamaged, and correctly connected. If replacing a damaged or blocked disposable accessory resolves the problem, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Applicator
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible APC accessory when available and safe for bench testing. Expected outcome: Normal ignition and stable operation with the known-good accessory isolate the original applicator or cable as the cause.

steps.title: 8. Verify Activation Control
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended hand switch or footswitch is detected, assigned correctly, and provides continuous activation rather than intermittent commands. Expected outcome: Activation remains stable throughout the test and is directed to the APC function as intended.

steps.title: 9. Perform Approved APC Functional Testing
steps.instructions: Using the appropriate ERBE procedure and approved test arrangement, confirm consistent APC activation and gas delivery. Do not perform open, improvised plasma testing or direct argon flow toward personnel. Expected outcome: APC starts consistently and operates normally within the approved verification procedure. Troubleshooting can stop if all required checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Ignition or Flow Instability
steps.instructions: If known-good accessories, verified argon supply, proper connections, and correct activation do not resolve the problem, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The VIO/APC system is removed from service for qualified pneumatic, electronic, or communication evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported delayed APC ignition and intermittent operation from the VIO 3 workstation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged APC applicator connection, while the workstation operated consistently with a known-good compatible applicator.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the defective applicator from use and verified reliable APC activation and stable system operation with approved testing.

helpfulDetails: Ignition behavior before and after correction

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - APC, Smoke Evacuation, or Workstation Communication Is Lost
description: Troubleshoots communication loss between the VIO 3 and connected workstation components such as APC or smoke-evacuation equipment.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Patient Safety and Required Surgical Functions
steps.instructions: If loss of communication affects electrosurgery, APC, smoke evacuation, or another required procedure function, transition to verified alternate equipment or an approved standalone workflow before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Clinical care continues without relying on a partially communicating workstation.

steps.title: 2. Identify Which Component Is Offline
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves the VIO 3, APC 3, IES 3, another connected component, or the entire workstation. Record which devices remain powered and what the VIO 3 displays. ERBE identifies APC 3 and IES 3 as systems that integrate with the VIO platform. [en.erbe-med.com](https://en.erbe-med.com/en-en/erbe-service/product-codes/?cHash=60340255dfc4c08ea96a12a725ab7416\&tx_erbeclassification_classifications%5Baction%5D=list\&tx_erbeclassification_classifications%5Bcontroller%5D=Classification\&tx_erbeclassification_classifications%5BshowAll%5D=1\&utm_source=chatgpt.com) Expected outcome: The communication failure is narrowed to a component or connection path.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power to Every Workstation Component
steps.instructions: Confirm each device is connected to appropriate AC power, switched on, and showing normal startup status. Inspect power cords and any approved workstation power distribution connections externally. Expected outcome: Every required component powers normally. Restore a lost power source if that alone caused the communication failure.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Communication Connections
steps.instructions: With the system safely out of clinical use, inspect accessible interconnect cables for incomplete seating, bent connectors, damaged strain relief, contamination, pinch damage, or accidental disconnection. Do not open the units or modify internal cabling. Expected outcome: All external workstation connections are secure and undamaged. Reseating a loose approved connection restores communication when that was the cause.

steps.title: 5. Confirm the Correct Workstation Component Is Installed
steps.instructions: Verify that the connected module and accessories are intended for the VIO 3 workstation and that components have not been exchanged between rooms without the required configuration. Expected outcome: The connected devices match the intended workstation configuration.

steps.title: 6. Power-Cycle the Workstation Safely
steps.instructions: When no patient depends on the equipment, perform a normal shutdown and restart using the approved sequence for the installed components. Do not repeatedly interrupt power during boot. Expected outcome: All components complete startup and re-establish communication. If communication returns and remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Isolate the Affected Peripheral
steps.instructions: If practical within approved configuration, determine whether the VIO 3 operates normally as an ESU while one workstation peripheral remains unavailable. Do not alter service-level system topology solely for troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to the connected peripheral/communication path or determined to affect the VIO 3 itself.

steps.title: 8. Verify Related Accessories
steps.instructions: For APC, verify the compatible applicator/cable and required argon setup. For smoke evacuation, verify the approved tubing, filter or accessory setup, and applicable control connection. Expected outcome: The peripheral is not merely unavailable because a required external accessory is absent, incorrectly connected, or exhausted.

steps.title: 9. Perform Integrated Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting the connection, confirm the VIO 3 recognizes the applicable workstation component and that commanded functions operate normally using safe test methods. Expected outcome: Communication remains stable and the integrated function responds correctly. Troubleshooting can stop if all required checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Communication Loss
steps.instructions: If verified power, connections, accessories, and normal restart do not restore communication, remove the affected equipment from service. Expected outcome: An incompletely communicating workstation is not returned to clinical use as though it were fully functional.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 no longer communicated with the connected smoke-evacuation component.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external workstation communication cable partially disconnected at the peripheral.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and secured the connection, restarted the workstation normally, and verified stable communication and coordinated function.

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Cooling Fan or Internal Temperature Alarm Persists
description: Troubleshoots persistent cooling or temperature warnings caused by blocked airflow, environmental conditions, workstation placement, contamination, or internal cooling faults.

steps.title: 1. Stop Using an Overheating Generator
steps.instructions: If the VIO 3 reports a persistent temperature condition, shuts down, smells overheated, or becomes abnormally hot, discontinue clinical use and provide another verified ESU. Do not repeatedly reactivate the generator to see whether it will continue operating. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on equipment with uncertain thermal protection or cooling.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Document the displayed warning, whether the fan is running, whether shutdown occurred, how long the unit had been operating, and whether high-duty-cycle activation preceded the event. Expected outcome: The thermal complaint is characterized before the equipment cools or conditions change.

steps.title: 3. Inspect External Airflow
steps.instructions: Check accessible intake and exhaust areas for drapes, packaging, dust accumulation, cart components, cables, or other equipment blocking airflow. Do not insert tools into ventilation openings. Expected outcome: All ventilation openings have unrestricted airflow. If an obstruction is removed, allow the unit to return to normal conditions and proceed to verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Workstation Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm adequate space around ventilation areas and make sure another heat-producing device is not exhausting directly into the VIO 3. Expected outcome: The generator is positioned so normal cooling airflow is possible.

steps.title: 5. Check the Environment
steps.instructions: Determine whether the equipment has been operated in an unusually hot location, enclosed cabinet, direct heat source, or other abnormal environment. Do not invent acceptable temperature limits; consult current manufacturer documentation when limits must be evaluated. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions are suitable for operation. Correcting an abnormal environment may resolve the alarm.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for Contamination or Damage
steps.instructions: With the unit off and removed from clinical use, inspect ventilation openings and exterior surfaces for excessive dust, fluid residue, damaged panels, or evidence of impact. Do not remove covers for routine external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: No obvious external condition is interfering with cooling. Visible fluid ingress or structural damage requires escalation.

steps.title: 7. Listen to Fan Operation During Startup
steps.instructions: After the generator has safely cooled and external conditions are corrected, start it normally and observe for unusual fan noise, scraping, cycling, vibration, or lack of expected airflow. Expected outcome: Cooling operation sounds and feels normal externally. Abnormal fan behavior supports removal from service.

steps.title: 8. Test Under Controlled Bench Conditions
steps.instructions: Using approved electrosurgical test equipment, perform normal functional verification and observe whether the temperature warning returns during appropriate testing. Do not intentionally stress the generator beyond approved test conditions. Expected outcome: The generator completes verification without recurring thermal warnings. If the problem was clearly caused by an external airflow obstruction and does not recur, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Verify No Secondary Effects
steps.instructions: Confirm the display, output, alarms, accessories, and workstation communication remain normal after the thermal event. Expected outcome: No additional malfunction is present following the corrected condition.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Thermal Alarms
steps.instructions: If the alarm returns in a normal environment with unobstructed airflow, the fan is abnormal, or the unit becomes excessively hot, stop testing and remove it from service. Expected outcome: A possible internal cooling or temperature-monitoring fault receives qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported a temperature warning on the VIO 3 during a procedure.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that workstation supplies were blocking the generator's ventilation area and no internal fault was reproduced after restoring airflow.
CCR.Resolution: Cleared the ventilation area, repositioned the supplies, and verified normal cooling and electrosurgical operation during bench testing.

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Cut/Coag Output Is Inconsistent or Fails Calibration
description: Troubleshoots unstable or unacceptable CUT/COAG output by separating accessory, setup, activation, analyzer, connection, and generator-related causes.

steps.title: 1. Remove Questionable Output From Clinical Use
steps.instructions: If CUT or COAG performance is unreliable, discontinue use of that generator for patient treatment. Move the procedure to another verified ESU or approved alternative before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is not exposed to uncertain electrosurgical output.

steps.title: 2. Clarify the Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves CUT, COAG, monopolar, bipolar, one instrument, one mode, one socket, or all output. Record the selected settings and whether the complaint came from clinical performance or an analyzer test. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to a specific output path or identified as generator-wide.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Complete Accessory Path
steps.instructions: Check the active instrument, cable, adapter, connector, socket, and neutral-electrode path when monopolar operation is involved. Look for damaged insulation, loose plugs, contamination, bent contacts, or incompatible accessories. Expected outcome: The complete external energy path is compatible, intact, and securely connected. Correcting an obvious accessory fault may resolve the complaint.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Selected Program and Mode
steps.instructions: Verify that the displayed socket, CUT/COAG mode, effect, and user-selectable settings match the intended clinical setup. Compare with the expected approved configuration rather than changing settings simply to make the analyzer reading pass. Expected outcome: The generator is being tested in the correct mode and configuration.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Electrosurgical Analyzer Setup
steps.instructions: Inspect the analyzer leads, load connections, adapters, test cable routing, and analyzer configuration. Confirm that the analyzer and accessories are suitable for testing HF electrosurgical output. A poor test connection can mimic unstable generator output. Expected outcome: The test setup is repeatable and appropriate. If correcting the analyzer setup produces stable acceptable results, troubleshooting can stop after repeat testing.

steps.title: 6. Repeat the Test With Known-Good Test Accessories
steps.instructions: Use known-good analyzer cables, adapters, and compatible ESU accessories. Repeat the same measurement several times without changing multiple variables simultaneously. Expected outcome: Results are repeatable. A failure that disappears with replacement test accessories identifies an external test-path problem.

steps.title: 7. Compare Output Paths
steps.instructions: When appropriate, compare CUT versus COAG and available compatible output sockets using the same controlled test method. Do not interpret different modes as though they should produce identical readings. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to one mode/socket or confirmed across multiple output paths.

steps.title: 8. Check for Activation Instability
steps.instructions: Confirm that hand-control or footswitch activation remains continuously detected during the test. An intermittent switch, cable, or assignment can produce output that appears to drop out. Expected outcome: Activation indication remains stable throughout the commanded energy delivery. Replace a defective external activation accessory if identified.

steps.title: 9. Perform the Approved Output Verification
steps.instructions: Use the current ERBE procedure, approved electrosurgical analyzer, specified test loads, and applicable limits for the exact VIO 3 configuration. Do not invent limits or attempt unauthorized calibration adjustments. Expected outcome: Output meets the applicable manufacturer requirements. If it does, document the results and return the unit to service according to policy.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Failed or Unstable Output
steps.instructions: If output remains inconsistent or fails manufacturer verification with known-good accessories and a verified analyzer setup, stop troubleshooting externally. Expected outcome: The generator is removed from service for qualified service-level evaluation rather than adjusted without approved procedures.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported inconsistent coagulation performance from the VIO 3 during activation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced intermittent activation and found the connected hand-control instrument cable was defective while generator output remained stable with a known-good accessory.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the defective accessory from service and verified repeatable CUT and COAG performance with approved test equipment.

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Footswitch Is Not Detected or Activates the Wrong Socket
description: Troubleshoots missing footswitch detection, intermittent pedal operation, or incorrect socket activation caused by accessories, connections, or assignments.

steps.title: 1. Prevent Unintended Energy Activation
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot incorrect footswitch activation while connected for patient treatment. Disconnect the clinical energy path or move the case to verified alternate equipment before testing. Expected outcome: Footswitch testing cannot unintentionally deliver energy to a patient.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether the footswitch is completely undetected, intermittent, activates CUT instead of COAG, activates the wrong instrument/socket, or functions correctly in some programs but not others. Expected outcome: The complaint is clearly defined before assignments or accessories are changed.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Footswitch
steps.instructions: Check the pedals, housing, cable, strain relief, and connector for damage, contamination, binding, fluid ingress evidence, or crushed cable sections. Expected outcome: The footswitch is externally intact and pedals return normally. A physically damaged footswitch should be removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the footswitch fully to the intended generator connection. Inspect the receptacle externally for damage or debris. Expected outcome: The footswitch is securely seated and detected. If detection becomes stable after correcting a loose connection, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Intended Assignment
steps.instructions: Using only normal authorized controls, review which socket or instrument the footswitch is assigned to for the selected program. Confirm the clinical staff's expected activation matches the displayed assignment. Expected outcome: Pedal activation is assigned to the intended socket. If correcting an approved assignment resolves the issue, verify operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check the Selected Program
steps.instructions: Determine whether a different saved program or subprogram was selected when the unexpected activation occurred. Compare the current setup with the facility's intended configuration. Expected outcome: The correct program and intended footswitch relationship are confirmed.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Footswitch
steps.instructions: Connect a known-good compatible footswitch when available and repeat the test under safe bench conditions. Expected outcome: If the replacement operates correctly, remove the original footswitch from service. If the behavior remains, continue evaluating assignment and generator-side causes.

steps.title: 8. Test Each Pedal Deliberately
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate ESU analyzer or other safe approved test arrangement, verify each pedal independently and observe which function and socket indicate activation. Expected outcome: Each pedal commands only its intended function. Any cross-activation or intermittent behavior is reproducible and documented.

steps.title: 9. Verify Stable Operation After Correction
steps.instructions: Repeat multiple pedal activations while observing the selected socket and analyzer. Move the external cable gently at strain-relief areas to identify obvious intermittency without stressing it. Expected outcome: Detection and assignment remain stable through repeated activation. Troubleshooting can stop if all required verification passes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Generator-Side or Persistent Assignment Problems
steps.instructions: If known-good footswitches remain undetected, activations route incorrectly despite verified assignments, or the receptacle is damaged, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The generator is removed from service for qualified evaluation rather than used with unpredictable activation control.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 footswitch activated a different socket than the instrument they intended to use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the selected program had the footswitch assigned to a different socket while the footswitch itself tested normally.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the approved socket assignment and verified correct CUT and COAG pedal activation with an electrosurgical analyzer.

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Generator Will Not Boot, Unexpectedly Restarts, or Shows a Persistent System Error
description: Troubleshoots startup failure, spontaneous restarting, or persistent system errors caused by power, cords, peripherals, environment, or generator-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Remove the Generator From Clinical Dependence
steps.instructions: If the VIO 3 fails to boot, restarts unexpectedly, or displays a persistent system error, do not continue using it during patient care. Provide another verified ESU. Expected outcome: Clinical treatment no longer depends on an unstable generator.

steps.title: 2. Document the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Record whether the unit is completely dead, begins startup and stops, repeatedly restarts, operates until activation, or reaches the normal screen with an error. Record the exact displayed message rather than paraphrasing it. Expected outcome: The startup or system failure is clearly characterized for later comparison and escalation.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Power Cord and Generator
steps.instructions: Check the AC cord, plug, strain relief, power inlet, exterior panels, and accessible connectors for damage, fluid exposure, overheating, or impact. If there is burning odor, visible fluid ingress, melted material, or significant physical damage, do not energize the generator again. Expected outcome: No external condition makes further testing unsafe. Unsafe physical findings trigger immediate removal from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the AC Source
steps.instructions: Test the receptacle with approved equipment or move the VIO 3 to a known-good appropriate outlet. If mounted on a workstation, include the approved cart power path in the evaluation. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is confirmed. If the generator boots normally on the verified source, investigate the original AC path separately.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Power Cord
steps.instructions: Substitute a known-good compatible power cord when appropriate. Expected outcome: The generator powers and remains stable with a verified cord, identifying the original cord as defective if the failure disappears.

steps.title: 6. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: With the generator off, disconnect nonessential external instruments, footswitches, communication peripherals, and workstation accessories that can safely be removed for bench evaluation. Expected outcome: The generator can be tested in a simplified external configuration. If it now starts normally, reconnect accessories one at a time to isolate the external trigger.

steps.title: 7. Attempt One Controlled Startup
steps.instructions: Connect the VIO 3 to verified AC power and perform a normal startup. Observe where the sequence stops and whether the same system message returns. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a failing generator. Expected outcome: The unit either boots normally or produces a repeatable failure suitable for documentation.

steps.title: 8. Check for Activation-Related Restarting
steps.instructions: If the unit starts normally but restarts when CUT or COAG is activated, evaluate it only with an approved electrosurgical analyzer and known-good accessories. Confirm stable AC power and that the restart is not caused by an intermittent external connection. Expected outcome: The restart is either traced to an external power/accessory problem or reproduced as a generator-level fault.

steps.title: 9. Perform Complete Functional Verification if the Failure Clears
steps.instructions: If an external cause is corrected, verify repeated startup, display/control operation, instrument recognition, alarms, footswitch operation, and electrosurgical output using approved test equipment. Expected outcome: The generator starts repeatedly and performs all required functions without errors or resets. Troubleshooting can stop if all applicable verification passes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Errors or Restarting
steps.instructions: If the error returns, startup remains incomplete, or the VIO 3 restarts without an identified external cause, stop troubleshooting. Do not clear persistent system errors through unauthorized service menus or attempt board-level repair. Expected outcome: The generator is removed from service for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 unexpectedly restarted during setup and subsequently displayed a persistent system error.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced the restart on multiple verified AC sources with external accessories disconnected, indicating a generator-level fault requiring service evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed and labeled the VIO 3 Out of Service and routed it for qualified bench evaluation with the observed error information documented.

helpfulDetails: Point in startup where failure occurs
Evidence of fluid, heat, odor, or damage

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Instrument Assignment or Socket Configuration Will Not Save
description: Troubleshoots assignments or socket settings that revert, fail to store, or load unexpectedly because of program selection, permissions, workflow, or configuration faults.

steps.title: 1. Prevent Use With an Unverified Configuration
steps.instructions: If the generator does not retain the intended instrument or socket assignment, do not use it clinically until the active configuration has been confirmed. An unexpected assignment can result in the wrong output being activated. Expected outcome: Patient use is prevented until configuration behavior is predictable.

steps.title: 2. Define What Will Not Save
steps.instructions: Identify the exact program, subprogram, socket, instrument, activation assignment, or setting that reverts. Record the value before saving, the action used to save it, and what appears after changing programs or restarting. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and limited to a defined configuration item.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Program Is Being Edited
steps.instructions: Confirm that staff are modifying the intended program or subprogram rather than a temporary setup or another saved configuration. Expected outcome: The correct configuration context is being used. If the apparent loss was caused by reopening a different program, no device repair is required.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Connected Instrument and Socket
steps.instructions: Confirm the compatible instrument is connected to the intended socket and is recognized normally. The VIO 3 associates instrument detection and socket functionality with the connected interface. [register.erbe-med.com](https://register.erbe-med.com/productfinder/Marketingmaterialien/80116-939_ERBE_US_VIO_3__D165797.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) Expected outcome: Recognition is stable and configuration is not being altered because the expected instrument is absent or connected elsewhere.

steps.title: 5. Check for Conflicting Activation Assignments
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible footswitch or instrument activation assignments. Make sure the intended socket is not being confused with another active socket or program. Expected outcome: The displayed assignment corresponds to the intended instrument and activation method.

steps.title: 6. Repeat the Save Workflow Deliberately
steps.instructions: Using the authorized workflow, make one controlled change, save it as intended, leave the configuration screen, and then reopen it. Do not modify multiple settings simultaneously. Expected outcome: The single change remains stored. If so, repeat as needed to confirm that the reported issue was workflow-related rather than a device fault.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With the generator removed from patient use, shut it down normally, restart it, and reload the same approved configuration. Expected outcome: The saved assignment remains unchanged after restart. If it reverts, document exactly which field or program is affected.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Another Approved Program
steps.instructions: Without altering protected configuration, determine whether other existing programs retain their settings normally. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to one program/configuration or shown to affect stored settings broadly.

steps.title: 9. Verify Functional Behavior, Not Just the Display
steps.instructions: Using appropriate test equipment, confirm that the socket and activation controls actually correspond to the displayed assignment after the configuration is reloaded. Expected outcome: Displayed and actual activation assignments agree. Troubleshooting can stop if the approved configuration is retained and verified.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Configuration Loss
steps.instructions: If configuration repeatedly reverts, cannot be stored, changes without user action, or displayed assignments do not match actual activation, remove the VIO 3 from service. Expected outcome: A generator with unreliable stored configuration is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 repeatedly loaded the wrong footswitch-to-socket assignment when their procedure program was selected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that staff had been editing a different subprogram than the one routinely loaded for the procedure.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the approved assignment in the intended program and verified that it remained stored after restart and activated the proper socket during testing.

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Instrument or Socket Module Is Not Recognized
description: Troubleshoots instruments or socket connections that are not detected, focusing on accessories, connector condition, socket selection, configuration, and external connection faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Surgical Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable electrosurgical connection while a patient depends on it. If the problem occurs during a procedure, move to an approved alternate generator, instrument, or technique according to clinical protocol before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without dependence on the questionable VIO 3 or instrument connection. Stop troubleshooting clinically if safe continuity cannot be maintained.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Exactly What Is Not Recognized
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem follows one instrument, one cable, one socket, one procedure program, or every connection. Record any displayed message and whether the instrument appears briefly and then disappears. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to an instrument/accessory, specific socket, configuration, or generator-wide recognition problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Instrument and Cable
steps.instructions: Disconnect the accessory and inspect the plug, cable, strain relief, pins or contacts, and instrument connection for contamination, moisture, bending, cracking, or physical damage. Verify the instrument and cable are intended for the installed VIO 3 socket configuration. Do not force an incompatible connector into a socket. Expected outcome: The accessory is compatible, clean, dry, undamaged, and seats normally. If replacing a damaged or incorrect accessory restores recognition, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Reseat the Connection
steps.instructions: Reconnect the instrument fully and observe whether the VIO 3 detects the connection. Confirm the selected instrument or procedure program corresponds to the intended socket. The VIO 3 uses instrument and plug detection as part of its socket interface, so incomplete insertion can prevent correct recognition. [register.erbe-med.com](https://register.erbe-med.com/productfinder/Marketingmaterialien/80116-939_ERBE_US_VIO_3__D165797.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) Expected outcome: The instrument is consistently recognized without manipulating the cable or connector. If recognition is restored and remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Instrument or Cable
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible accessory of the same intended type when available. Test only within normal Clinical Engineering verification practices. Expected outcome: If the known-good accessory works normally, remove the original accessory from use and document the finding. If neither accessory is recognized, continue troubleshooting the VIO 3 connection path.

steps.title: 6. Compare Available Sockets When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the device configuration provides another compatible socket intended for the same accessory type, compare recognition behavior without changing restricted configuration. Do not use an incompatible socket merely for testing. Expected outcome: A problem isolated to one socket suggests a socket/interface or configuration issue. Normal operation on all appropriate sockets suggests the original accessory was the likely cause.

steps.title: 7. Verify Program and Socket Assignment
steps.instructions: Check the normal user-accessible program and instrument assignment. Confirm the selected setup is intended for the connected instrument and that no unintended saved program is directing the workflow to another socket. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or change protected configuration. Expected outcome: The intended instrument and socket are correctly associated. If correcting an approved user-level selection restores detection, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Socket Externally
steps.instructions: With the generator removed from clinical use, inspect the affected socket for debris, fluid contamination, deformation, damaged contacts, looseness, or evidence of forced insertion. Do not disassemble the socket assembly. Expected outcome: The socket is externally intact and clean. Physical socket damage requires removal from service and escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using approved accessories and appropriate electrosurgical test equipment when required, confirm stable instrument recognition, correct socket identification, normal activation indication, alarms, and expected output behavior. Expected outcome: Recognition remains stable through repeated connect/disconnect and functional checks. If successful, the generator may be returned to service according to facility policy.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good compatible accessories are not recognized, recognition is intermittent, or a socket is physically damaged, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The VIO 3 is removed from service for qualified evaluation rather than being returned with an unreliable instrument interface.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 would not recognize the connected electrosurgical instrument.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the instrument cable connector was damaged and recognition returned consistently with a known-good compatible cable.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the damaged cable from service, connected the approved replacement, and verified stable instrument recognition and normal generator operation.

helpfulDetails: Whether the problem followed the accessory
Recognition behavior before and after correction

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Neutral-Electrode Safety Alarm Persists
description: Troubleshoots persistent neutral-electrode safety alarms caused by electrode application, cable connections, incompatible accessories, damaged cables, or generator-side detection problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Testing
steps.instructions: Do not attempt monopolar activation while the neutral-electrode safety condition is unresolved. If the patient requires continued electrosurgery, provide another verified generator or approved clinical alternative. Expected outcome: No monopolar energy is delivered through a system with an unresolved return-electrode safety condition.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Alarm Condition
steps.instructions: Record the exact displayed neutral-electrode indication or message and determine whether the alarm appears immediately when connecting the electrode, after patient application, or intermittently during use. Expected outcome: The alarm pattern is clearly identified before accessories are changed.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Neutral Electrode and Cable
steps.instructions: Confirm that the neutral electrode and connecting cable are compatible with the VIO 3 and appropriate for the selected application. Inspect the cable, plug, connector, and electrode connection for damage, contamination, or incomplete engagement. ERBE specifies that neutral-electrode compatibility and cable suitability must be verified for the VIO system being used. [register.erbe-med.com](https://register.erbe-med.com/productfinder/Marketingmaterialien/80115-501_ERBE_EN_VIO_3_V_14x__D247327.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) Expected outcome: A compatible, undamaged electrode and cable are connected securely. If the alarm clears after correcting the accessory connection, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Correct Patient Application
steps.instructions: Clinical personnel should confirm that the electrode is applied according to the approved clinical procedure, including full contact and appropriate orientation. The VIO 3 NESSY system evaluates the return-electrode connection and, with compatible split electrodes, patient contact characteristics. [register.erbe-med.com](https://register.erbe-med.com/productfinder/Marketingmaterialien/80116-939_ERBE_US_VIO_3__D165797.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) Clinical Engineering should not repeatedly manipulate a patient-applied electrode while the device is being actively used. Expected outcome: Proper application produces an acceptable neutral-electrode status. If the alarm clears, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Neutral-Electrode Cable
steps.instructions: If permitted and clinically appropriate, replace the cable with a known-good compatible cable. Inspect both cable ends carefully before connection. Expected outcome: If the alarm clears with the replacement cable, remove the original cable from service and document the failure.

steps.title: 6. Test Away From the Patient
steps.instructions: If the alarm persists and the procedure can safely transition to alternate equipment, remove the VIO 3 from clinical use and evaluate it on the bench using approved ERBE-compatible accessories or approved test equipment. Do not bypass the neutral-electrode safety system. Expected outcome: The alarm behavior can be reproduced safely without relying on a patient connection.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Neutral-Electrode Socket
steps.instructions: Inspect the generator-side neutral-electrode receptacle for contamination, bent or recessed contacts, looseness, cracking, or foreign material. Do not insert improvised probes or defeat socket interlocks. Expected outcome: The receptacle is clean and mechanically intact. Visible damage requires escalation.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Known-Good Compatible Accessories
steps.instructions: Connect approved known-good neutral-electrode test accessories as appropriate to the facility's test method. Expected outcome: Normal status with known-good accessories identifies the original accessory path as the cause. A persistent alarm with verified accessories points toward a generator-side fault.

steps.title: 9. Verify Alarm and Functional Operation
steps.instructions: After correction, confirm that the normal neutral-electrode indication is present and that disconnecting or producing an approved simulated unsafe condition causes the expected safety response using appropriate test methods. Expected outcome: The safety system accepts a proper connection and responds correctly to a simulated fault. Troubleshooting can stop if all required tests pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent NESSY-Related Failure
steps.instructions: If the VIO 3 continues to indicate an unsafe neutral-electrode condition with verified accessories and approved testing, remove it from service. Expected outcome: A generator with unreliable return-electrode monitoring is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 continued to display a neutral-electrode safety alarm after connecting the patient return electrode.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an intermittent neutral-electrode cable connection that failed comparison with a known-good compatible cable.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective cable and verified normal neutral-electrode detection and safety-alarm response with approved testing.

title: ERBE VIO 3 Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) - Touchscreen, Display, or Control Panel Freezes During Setup
description: Troubleshoots frozen, delayed, or unresponsive user controls caused by contamination, accessories, power conditions, software state, or control-interface failure.

steps.title: 1. Remove an Unresponsive Generator From Active Use
steps.instructions: If the controls freeze during a case and settings or status cannot be confirmed reliably, use another verified ESU. Do not continue operating a generator with uncertain control response. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on the unresponsive user interface.

steps.title: 2. Characterize the Freeze
steps.instructions: Determine whether the entire display is frozen or only touch input is affected. Note whether physical controls respond, whether displayed values continue updating, and what operation immediately preceded the failure. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as display, touch input, control-panel, or broader system unresponsiveness.

steps.title: 3. Inspect and Clean the External Interface
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen and surrounding controls for fluid, cleaning residue, adhesive, drapes, protective material, or physical damage. Clean only according to approved facility/manufacturer practices. Expected outcome: The interface is clean, dry, unobstructed, and physically intact. If normal operation returns, continue with repeat verification.

steps.title: 4. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Once safely on the bench, disconnect nonessential external accessories and peripherals that can be removed without changing system configuration. Leave required test connections in place. Expected outcome: The VIO 3 can be evaluated independently of a potentially problematic external accessory or workstation connection.

steps.title: 5. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Check the power cord, plug, receptacle, and any approved cart power connection. Test the outlet or use a verified power source if power quality is questionable. Expected outcome: Stable AC power is confirmed. If changing to a verified source eliminates freezing, investigate the original power path separately.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With no patient attached and no active energy delivery, shut down the generator normally and restart it. Do not repeatedly cycle power or interrupt startup. Expected outcome: The VIO 3 boots normally and the touchscreen/control panel becomes responsive. If so, continue testing rather than immediately returning it to service.

steps.title: 7. Reproduce the Original Setup Sequence
steps.instructions: Repeat the normal setup actions that preceded the freeze, including program selection and connecting the relevant compatible accessory. Do not access restricted diagnostic or service menus. Expected outcome: Controls remain responsive through the previously problematic workflow. A repeatable freeze establishes an unresolved fault.

steps.title: 8. Observe for Accessory-Dependent Behavior
steps.instructions: Reconnect external components one at a time when appropriate and observe whether a particular accessory, peripheral, or workstation connection consistently precedes the freeze. Expected outcome: Either one external connection is isolated as the trigger or the VIO 3 freezes independently.

steps.title: 9. Complete Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify display response, touch input, program selection, instrument recognition, alarm presentation, and safe activation using approved test equipment. Expected outcome: The interface remains stable and all intended controls function normally. If the original problem cannot be reproduced after correcting an identifiable external cause, document and return to service according to policy.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Freezing
steps.instructions: If the interface freezes again, displays incorrect information, loses input intermittently, or requires repeated rebooting, remove the VIO 3 from service. Expected outcome: An intermittently unreliable control interface is not returned to the OR.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the VIO 3 touchscreen stopped responding while they were setting up the generator.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found heavy dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen; the generator remained responsive after the residue was removed.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the touchscreen according to approved procedure and verified repeated setup, control response, alarms, and normal functional operation.

helpfulDetails: Screen image at time of freeze
